title: Halving past any target
line: A bar of length 1 keeps halving beside a tiny 0.01 rod, and a counter shows it slips below after 7 cuts.

title: More than half, or not enough
line: Two bars of length 2: one loses over half of what's left and vanishes; the other loses 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 and stalls above 1.

title: The square's diagonal never stops
line: Subtract a square's side from its diagonal; the leftovers form a smaller square and diagonal, so the subtraction repeats forever, zooming in.

title: One race ends, one doesn't
line: Rods 7 and 5 subtract down to a common unit in four steps, while a square's side and diagonal keep subtracting forever.

title: Rods that find their common unit
line: Rods of 21 and 15 chop each other in turn: 21 leaves 6, 15 leaves 3, and 3 fits 6 exactly.

title: Carving a rectangle into squares
line: A 12 by 9 rectangle loses its biggest square, then the next biggest, until only 3 by 3 squares remain, tiling it exactly.

title: Shrinking the ruler to fit
line: A ruler's ticks shrink until rods of 1.5 and 2.5 both end exactly on a tick, at spacing 0.5: ratio 3 to 5.

title: Squares on rods, square numbers
line: Rods of 2 and 3 grow squares of 4 and 9 tiles; a side and diagonal grow areas 1 and 2, and 2 isn't square.

title: Rectangle that falls short by a square
line: A point slides along a line of 10; the rectangle x by (10 − x) reshapes as its area traces a parabola peaking at 25.

title: An L of dots that's a square
line: An L of 9 dots wraps a 4 by 4 grid into a 5 by 5 square; 9 is square, so 3, 4, 5 appears.

title: Folding a rectangle around a square
line: An 8 by 2 rectangle of tiles splits and folds around a 3 by 3 square into a 5 by 5: 16 + 9 = 25.

title: Polygons grow with diameter squared
line: A lopsided pentagon in a circle scales as the diameter goes 1, 2, 3, and its area counter reads 1, 4, 9.

title: Doubling sides toward the circle
line: A square in a unit circle doubles to 8, 16, 32, 64 sides while its area counter climbs from 2.00 toward 3.14.

title: Two circles, one ratio
line: Circles of diameter 2 and 3 get matching polygons with ever more sides; the area ratio counter stays locked at 4/9.

title: Each sliver loses over half
line: Zoom into one sliver between a circle and a square; the triangle that fills it on doubling always covers more than half.

title: Polygon squeezed between two circles
line: A square, octagon, 16-gon, then 32-gon fill a circle of radius 1 until one finally clears an inner circle of radius 0.9.

title: Five squares make one
line: Five unit squares in a plus sign are cut and slid into one square, whose side is a golden cut's long piece plus 1.

title: Hunting for exactly five
line: A cut point slides along a line of length 2; the counter for (long piece + 1)² hits exactly 5 at the golden cut.

title: Two squares fill three
line: Squares on a golden-cut line and on its short piece pour their area into three squares on the long piece, filling them exactly.

title: A golden line keeps growing
line: A golden-cut line gains its long piece again and again, growing 1, 1.618, 2.618, 4.236, while its ratio counter never budges.

title: Golden rectangle adds a square
line: A golden rectangle grows a square on its long side, again and again, while quarter-circle arcs in each square trace a spiral.

title: Locking a floppy pentagon
line: A pentagon of five equal hinged sticks wobbles through lopsided shapes until three angles match, then snaps into the regular pentagon.

title: Diagonals cut in golden ratio
line: Two pentagon diagonals cross; the longer piece of one swings onto a side and matches it exactly, and the ratio reads 1.618.

title: Pentagrams all the way down
line: A pentagram leaves a small upside-down pentagon inside; draw its star, then again, zooming in, each shrinking by the same factor.

title: Hexagon plus decagon
line: A hexagon and decagon share a circle; one side of each lies end to end, and the joint lands exactly on the golden cut.

title: Three polygons, one right triangle
line: Sides of a pentagon, hexagon, and decagon in one circle lift off and snap into a right triangle, squares on each side adding up.

title: Triangle side squared is three radii
line: From a triangle's corner in a circle a diameter appears; the leftover chord equals a radius, so 4 radius-squares minus 1 leaves 3.

title: Octahedron's diameter, drawn flat
line: An octahedron's middle four corners form a square in a circle; two squares on its side slide over to fill the diameter's square.

title: Cube diagonal in two hops
line: Flat right triangles hop from a cube's side 1 to face diagonal √2 to body diagonal √3, the sphere's diameter.

title: Five solid edges on one semicircle
line: Edges of the five regular solids for one sphere appear as chords on one semicircle, then line up as bars, longest to shortest.

title: Why only five regular solids
line: Triangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons crowd around a point while a gap-angle counter shows which fold into a corner and which lie flat.
